_comment: AGENT: always read this file via the task-index-manager skill before reading or writing any task state. System tracker for ai-worldbuilder (ADR 002).

tasks.title: Live check of cell_registry.py reconcile in the bakeoff world
tasks.notes: reconcile (task 44) is tested only with fakes. With the bakeoff world open and MCP up, on a throwaway patch (e.g. the 4x4 ghost patch at x 6128-6131, z -5546..-5543 in cell 47,-44; use stage 'other' applies): (1) `cell_registry.py reconcile` on a healthy world exits 0 and prints clean, also `reconcile 47,-44`; (2) break one planned block with a block_fill_batch (air, then another block); dry run exits 1, shows missing/foreign with the right want/got sample, changes no blocks, writes no journal line, claims no lock; (3) `reconcile 47,-44 --fix` re-fills, exits 0, a rerun is clean, the journal gains a `repair` line; (4) crash an apply between fills and Ticket.finish (patch cell_journal.Ticket.finish to raise): `site_recover.py status` and `reconcile` both show it in flight, and recover lands or rolls back as before; (5) `reconcile --fix` with the lock held by another owner is refused with a SystemExit. Clean up test entries afterwards (CellRegistry.reset() archives the journal; delete any recover_test_* files). Nothing in this check copies or edits region files: blocks change over MCP only. Earlier session scripts are not kept; the old recover test is described in task 42's archive note. ALSO (audit finding F2, now answerable): the reconnected minecraft_world MCP server lists block read tools: block_get_state, block_scan_region, block_scan_summary, block_get_top_y (plus block_render_region, block_fill_*, structure_*). Read their schemas and limits with `python3 scripts/mcp.py tools/list` (box size cap, palette/index output, cost per call against the 60 requests/minute pacing in mc_paced.py), time a bulk scan_region read of one 128x128 cell column set, and record the result in docs/audits/region-block-reads.md. If a bulk read is fast and exact, file a task to give LiveBlocks an MCP backend (ADR 004 'Block read path': callers do not change) and drop the region-file parser; if not, keep the guarded region reader and say why.

tasks.title: Journal signs and entities so reconcile/recover can restore them
tasks.notes: Code review #50 (range 37e905e^..HEAD). site_kit.apply writes signs/entities via McpWriter after block fills, but CellRegistry only journals block cells (site_kit.py comment ~542-543). reconcile --fix re-commits blocks only; site_recover land/rollback cannot recreate sign text or summoned entities. ADR 004 'one journal' for applies that use Plan.sign/entity is incomplete until these are recorded (or explicitly out of scope with a loud refuse when a plan has them).

tasks.title: After undo rollback, clear journal undone so views match the world
tasks.notes: Code review #50. Known quirk from #42 Cut site_kit.apply over to the journal: when recover rolls back an apply that followed a landed Undo (restoring the pre-undo world via structure backup), the journal still marks the original pass undone. Ownership/views then disagree with the restored blocks. Need a journal finish/repair path that un-voids the undone targets when that rollback path runs (or refuse undo+structure combinations that cannot stay consistent).

tasks.title: Refuse apply onto aborted journal entry with a clear in-flight message
tasks.notes: Code review #50. Known quirk from #42: apply onto an aborted (begun, unfinished) entry is refused by the ownership Clash check rather than InFlight / a begun-entry message, so agents get 'cells belong to earlier builds' instead of being pointed at site_recover.py. Align Clash vs InFlight ordering (or treat begun owners as in-flight) so the recovery path is obvious.

tasks.title: site_recover soft-fails on broad Exception; tighten to loud typed errors
tasks.notes: Code review #50 vs ADR 004 loud-errors. site_recover.recover catches bare Exception around reconcile/flush and around structure restore, sets action=unsure/failed, prints, and returns without re-raising (site_recover.py ~160 and ~227). Recovery UX wants a dry-run report, but the catch is wider than JournalError/OSError and can hide unexpected bugs. Narrow the except clauses and let unexpected errors propagate.
